findings.issue_text: [BUG] addGuestsHandler calls eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees(evt, booking), a method this diff never defines anywhere and that does not exist on EventManager at the base commit - no code before this feature ever called it. The TypeScript build fails with TS2339 (Property updateCalendarAttendees does not exist on type EventManager); if forced through anyway, every add-guests mutation rejects with 'TypeError: eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees is not a function' after the attendees have already been written to the database.

[BUG] The team-permission check ANDs isTeamAdmin and isTeamOwner, requiring a user to hold both roles at once - impossible for a membership that carries a single role - so isTeamAdminOrOwner is false for every team admin. A team admin (and, if isTeamAdmin matches only the ADMIN role, the owner too) who picks 'Additional Guests' on a team booking gets a 403 you_do_not_have_permission; the admin-or-owner access this branch was named to grant never works.

[BUG] uniqueGuests filters the input only against existing attendees and the blacklist, never against duplicates within the input list, and the server schema in addGuests.schema.ts omits the uniqueness refine the client copy enforces, so the same email submitted twice survives filtering and createMany inserts it twice. A direct addGuests mutation with guests ['a@x.com','a@x.com'] creates two identical BookingAttendee rows, sends the guest two scheduled emails with two ICS attachments, and permanently corrupts the booking's attendee list.

[BUG] The attendee createMany is committed outside any transaction and before the un-guarded eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees call at line 165, so a calendar-API failure leaves the database write applied while the mutation returns an error. When the calendar update throws, the user sees 'Unable to add guests' even though the guests are already persisted; the retry then fails with BAD_REQUEST emails_must_be_unique_valid because the addresses are now existing attendees, leaving a half-updated booking (rows in DB, no calendar sync, no emails) and a user stuck on a misleading error.

[BUG] The EventManager is constructed from the requesting user's credentials (getUsersCredentials(ctx.user)) instead of the booking organizer's, so for any caller who is not the organizer the calendar lookup runs against the wrong user's connected calendars. A team admin or attendee adding guests to another user's booking gets a success toast while the organizer's Google/Outlook event silently never receives the new attendees - the sync no-ops because no credential matches the booking's references.

[BUG] The mutation's onSuccess resets multiEmailValue but never resets isInvalidEmail, and the dialog component stays mounted after closing, so the validation-error flag outlives a successful add. A user who triggers the 'Emails must be unique and valid' error, corrects the address, and adds guests successfully sees the same red error pre-rendered on the empty form the next time they open Add Guests for any booking.

[BUG] sendAddGuestsEmails is passed the raw input guests rather than uniqueGuests, so the newGuests.includes(attendee.email) check in email-manager.ts classifies already-existing attendees whose address was re-submitted as newly added. An existing attendee whose email was re-typed receives a duplicate AttendeeScheduledEmail ('you are scheduled') instead of the 'new guests added' notice, and blacklisted addresses that were filtered out of the database write still steer which template each attendee gets.

[BUG] Blacklist entries are lowercased but the guest address is compared verbatim (blacklistedGuestEmails.includes(guest)) and the existing-attendee check is case-sensitive (guest === attendee.email), so both guards are defeated by case variation. Submitting USER@EXAMPLE.COM bypasses BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS entirely, and A@x.com plus a@x.com both pass the filter and create two attendee rows for the same person.

[BUG] The handler fetches the booking with no status filter and never checks booking.status, while BookingListItem.tsx adds the 'Additional Guests' menu item unconditionally, so guests can be added to CANCELLED and REJECTED bookings. Guests of a cancelled booking receive 'Guests Added' and 'scheduled' emails carrying a CONFIRMED ICS invitation for an event that no longer exists, and the cancelled booking's attendee list is mutated as if it were active.

[BUG] The CalendarEvent handed to sendAddGuestsEmails never sets team, so calendarEvent.team is always undefined and the team-member notification loop added in email-manager.ts can never execute for any booking. For team and round-robin bookings, team members never receive the add-guests notification the new email-manager branch was written to send - the loop is dead code for exactly the bookings it targets.

[ADVISORY] The catch block discards the caught error object and logs only the literal string 'Error sending AddGuestsEmails'. When guest-notification emails fail (SMTP outage, template crash), production logs carry no reason and no stack while the mutation still returns success - the operator cannot diagnose why guests never heard anything.

[ADVISORY] The diff introduces the BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS environment variable but adds no .env.example entry, docs note, or typed-env registration for it. Operators have no discoverable way to learn the guest-email blacklist exists; the knob ships inert because nobody outside this source file can find it.

[ADVISORY] The dialog hand-rolls a second ZAddGuestsInputSchema (with a uniqueness refine) that drifts from the server's addGuests.schema.ts, which has no refine - two same-named validators for one payload maintained in different packages. Guest validation rules now live in two places under one name; the drift is already load-bearing (the server's missing refine is what lets duplicate attendee rows through), and the next rule change must be applied twice or the UI and API silently disagree.

[ADVISORY] The entire addGuests mutation - permission matrix, blacklist filtering, dedupe, and calendar sync - plus the AddGuestsDialog client state machine ship with zero tests in the diff. The AND-for-OR permission bug and the duplicate-email insertion are precisely the regressions a permission-matrix and schema test would have caught; every future refactor of this handler ships unverified.

[ADVISORY] The remove-button tooltip hardcodes the English literal 'Remove email' instead of using t(), unlike every sibling string in the new components. Non-English users see an untranslated English tooltip inside an otherwise localized dialog.

[ADVISORY] The permission gate grants every attendee of a booking - any past booker whose email matches - the right to add arbitrary guests, with no rate limit and no organizer confirmation. Any user who has ever been a guest on a booking can repeatedly inject arbitrary email addresses into the organizer's calendar event and trigger notification emails from the instance, a spam vector against organizers.

[BUG] The permission check joins the two role tests with && so the caller must be BOTH a team admin AND a team owner, contradicting the variable name isTeamAdminOrOwner which declares OR semantics. A team ADMIN who is not the team owner is rejected with FORBIDDEN you_do_not_have_permission when adding guests to a teammate's booking — exactly the user class this branch was written to admit; if isTeamAdmin does not include the OWNER role the expression is always false and only organizers/attendees can ever use the feature.

[BUG] The booking is fetched with no condition or subsequent check on booking.status or booking.endTime, so the mutation accepts CANCELLED, REJECTED, unconfirmed PENDING and already-ended bookings. Guests added to a cancelled booking are persisted as attendees on a dead booking, updateCalendarAttendees runs against the organizer's calendar event for it, and every guest is emailed an ICS with status CONFIRMED for an event that is cancelled, not yet confirmed, or already over.

[BUG] The CalendarEvent literal never sets a team field, so calendarEvent.team?.members in sendAddGuestsEmails (packages/emails/email-manager.ts:531-537) is always undefined and the team-member notification loop is unreachable dead code. For collective and round-robin team bookings, fellow team members never receive the OrganizerAddGuestsEmail notification this same diff implements — the notification requirement the loop encodes is silently dropped, and the branch ships untested and untriggerable.

[BUG] The EventManager is built from the requesting user's credentials (getUsersCredentials(ctx.user)) instead of the booking organizer's, yet updateCalendarAttendees must modify the organizer's calendar event. When the caller is an attendee or team admin — the classes the permission gate at lines 54-56 explicitly admits — their credential list contains no match for the organizer's destinationCalendar credentialId, so the calendar attendee update silently no-ops and Google/Outlook attendee lists permanently diverge from the booking.

[BUG] ZAddGuestsInputSchema validates email format but drops the uniqueness requirement that the client-side refine in AddGuestsDialog.tsx:26-29 enforces, leaving the directly callable tRPC mutation without it. An authenticated caller posting guests: ["a@x.com","a@x.com"] passes the server schema, and the handler filter (which only compares against existing attendees) inserts two identical BookingAttendee rows and sends the same guest two AttendeeScheduledEmail invitations.

[BUG] The dedup/blacklist filter compares emails case-sensitively (guest === attendee.email and blacklistedGuestEmails.includes(guest)) while the blacklist is lowercased and guest input is never normalized. Submitting User@Example.com when user@example.com is already an attendee bypasses the filter and creates a duplicate attendee record (duplicate emails and ICS entries), and the same casing trick bypasses the BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS blacklist entirely.

[BUG] For seats-based event types the handler passes seatsPerTimeSlot/seatsShowAttendees into evt (lines 145-146) but createMany inserts BookingAttendee rows with no BookingSeat linkage. Guests added to a seats booking occupy no seat, so seat counts no longer reflect actual attendees, overbooking past seatsPerTimeSlot becomes possible, and the seat cancellation and manage-seats flows cannot see or remove these orphaned attendee rows.

[BUG] The isAttendee permission check compares attendee.email === user.email case-sensitively. A booker whose attendee record was stored with different letter-casing than their login email (e.g. typed John@Mail.com into the booking form) is wrongfully FORBIDDEN from adding guests to their own booking.

[BUG] sendAddGuestsEmails is called with the raw guests input instead of the filtered uniqueGuests. An existing attendee who is re-listed in the guest input matches newGuests in email-manager.ts:541 and receives a fresh AttendeeScheduledEmail ('you are scheduled') instead of the AttendeeAddGuestsEmail notice — a duplicate booking confirmation for an event they already attend.

[BUG] When booking.userId is null the organizer lookup runs findFirstOrThrow({ id: booking.userId || 0 }), which throws a raw Prisma P2025 not-found error that no TRPCError wraps. Any booking row with a null userId (the || 0 guard exists because the field is nullable) crashes the mutation with an unhandled Prisma error surfaced as a generic 500 instead of a typed 4xx the dialog can display.

[BUG] onSuccess resets multiEmailValue but never resets isInvalidEmail, and the dialog component stays mounted inside BookingListItem so its state survives close/reopen. After a failed-then-corrected-then-successful add, reopening the dialog immediately shows the stale red 'Emails must be unique and valid' banner over an empty form.

[BUG] The remove-email Tooltip hardcodes the English string "Remove email" instead of using the t() function the component already imports and uses for add_another. Every non-English user sees an untranslated English tooltip on the remove button; the diff adds locale keys for all other new strings but silently drops this one.

[ADVISORY] The catch block discards the caught err and logs only a static string via console.log. When AddGuests email delivery fails, operators get no error object, stack trace, or recipient list — production email outages on this path are undiagnosable from logs while the user still sees the 'Guests added' success toast.

[ADVISORY] The diff adds a 174-line handler with a four-way permission matrix, dedup/blacklist filtering, a Prisma multi-insert, calendar sync and email fan-out plus a new dialog and two email templates, and none of the 15 touched files is a test file (no *.test.*, *.spec.*, __tests__/, test/ or e2e paths appear in the diff). The permission matrix — where the && vs || defect at lines 46-48 and the case-sensitive comparisons at lines 52 and 76 actually shipped — has zero regression coverage, so the next refactor of these checks can silently lock out organizers or admit strangers with no failing build.

[ADVISORY] ZAddGuestsInputSchema puts no upper bound on the guests array and the handler applies no count limit. A single authenticated request with a 10,000-entry guests array triggers a 10,000-row createMany and 10,000 outbound invitation emails — a mass-email primitive reachable on any booking the caller can see, with no rate limit specific to this mutation.

[ADVISORY] New guests are persisted with name: "" and then emailed through AttendeeScheduledEmail, whose payload addresses recipients as ${this.attendee.name} <${this.attendee.email}>. Every guest invitation is addressed with an empty display name (To: ' <email>') and carries an ICS attendee with CN="", degrading deliverability and making the feature's core invitation email look broken to the very people it exists to invite.

[BUG] isTeamAdminOrOwner joins isTeamAdmin and isTeamOwner with && instead of ||, so the permission holds only for users who are simultaneously admin and owner. A team admin who is not the team owner (and an owner who is not an admin) selecting 'additional_guests' on their team's booking receives FORBIDDEN you_do_not_have_permission, silently locking out the entire admin class the variable name promises to allow.

[BUG] The handler fetches the booking by id alone and never checks booking.status, so addGuests accepts CANCELLED and REJECTED bookings. The add_members menu item is added unconditionally to the dropdown options, so a user adds guests to a cancelled booking, the handler inserts attendee rows, sends 'Guests Added' emails carrying a status CONFIRMED .ics for an event that no longer exists, and runs updateCalendarAttendees against a dead booking's calendar references.

[BUG] The uniqueGuests filter only removes emails matching existing attendees and never deduplicates the input array itself, while the server schema (addGuests.schema.ts line 5) omits the uniqueness .refine that the client-side copy in AddGuestsDialog enforces. A direct addGuests mutation with ['a@b.com','a@b.com'] passes both gates and createMany inserts two Attendee rows with the same email, so the guest receives two identical scheduled-confirmation emails and appears twice on the calendar event — the uniqueness invariant exists only in the client schema, which any API caller bypasses.

[BUG] blacklistedGuestEmails entries are lowercased at line 71 but guest emails are compared un-normalized at line 77, and the existing-attendee duplicate check at line 76 is likewise case-sensitive. Submitting 'User@Example.com' against a blacklist entry 'user@example.com' bypasses the blacklist and creates the attendee anyway, and the same case variation defeats both the duplicate filter and the isAttendee permission comparison at line 52, leaving the handler's only abuse control trivially bypassable.

[BUG] The guests array has no .max() bound and the handler performs no volume check, while the permission model deliberately lets any booking attendee invoke the mutation. An authenticated attendee submits thousands of emails in one request and the handler creates an attendee row and dispatches a scheduled email for each plus a notification to every existing attendee, turning the organizer's booking into an unbounded spam amplifier with no count or rate limit anywhere on the path.

[BUG] The handler reads seatsPerTimeSlot into evt at line 145 but never enforces it before createMany, so guest additions bypass the seat-capacity invariant that the normal booking flow enforces. For a fully-booked seats event type, an organizer or attendee adds any number of guests and the handler inserts attendee rows past seatsPerTimeSlot, overbooking the seat-limited event that the seats feature exists to cap.

[BUG] getUsersCredentials is called with ctx.user and the EventManager is constructed from ...user (the requesting user), but the calendar event being updated belongs to booking.user, so whenever the caller is an attendee or team admin rather than the organizer the manager holds the wrong account's credentials. A non-organizer adding guests runs updateCalendarAttendees with credentials that hold no calendar app matching the booking's references, so the new guests never appear on the organizer's Google/Microsoft calendar event while the mutation reports 'Guests added' success.

[BUG] The CalendarEvent built for notifications omits the team field entirely, so calendarEvent.team in sendAddGuestsEmails (email-manager.ts lines 531-537) is always undefined and the team-member notification loop is dead code. For collective and round-robin team bookings, fellow team members never receive the OrganizerAddGuestsEmail this diff adds — only the organizer is notified — despite the email path existing specifically to include them.

[BUG] sendAddGuestsEmails is passed the raw input guests rather than the filtered uniqueGuests, so emails that were rejected (duplicates of existing attendees, blacklisted) still drive template selection in email-manager.ts. When the submitted list contains an existing attendee's email, that attendee matches newGuests.includes(...) and receives a full duplicate AttendeeScheduledEmail 'you are booked' confirmation instead of the AttendeeAddGuestsEmail notice, re-confirming an event they already hold.

[BUG] onSuccess resets multiEmailValue but never resets isInvalidEmail, and the only other reset path is the Cancel button, so the validation-error state survives both successful adds and ESC/X closes. After one failed validation followed by a successful add, reopening the dialog shows the 'Emails must be unique and valid' error banner over a fresh empty form, and the banner also stays up while the user is correcting the emails.

[BUG] The remove-action tooltip content is the hardcoded English string 'Remove email' while the adjacent add-action button uses t('add_another'). Every non-English user sees an untranslated English tooltip on the remove action inside an otherwise fully localized dialog.

[ADVISORY] The catch around sendAddGuestsEmails discards err and emits only a static string via console.log instead of the logger. When email delivery fails, guests are already persisted and the caller sees 'Guests added' success while no attendee receives any notification, and the operator troubleshooting it gets no error object, stack, or structured log entry — just a bare console line.

[ADVISORY] The diff ships 174 lines of permission, filtering, and mutation logic plus a new dialog and a new shared UI component with zero tests. The exact regression classes this diff already contains — the &&/|| permission operator, the case-sensitive blacklist, the missing status check — are guarded by nothing, so the next refactor of isTeamAdminOrOwner or the uniqueGuests filter ships or breaks silently.

[ADVISORY] BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS is a brand-new env-var-gated control introduced with no .env.example entry, documentation, or feature-flag surface anywhere in the diff. An operator who needs to block guest-email abuse has no way to discover the variable exists, so the only abuse control in the feature ships effectively inert in every deployment whose operator has not read this handler's source.

[ADVISORY] The bookings router gains only an addGuests mutation — no removeGuests and no guest-list read — while the feature is billed as guest management. An organizer who typos an email or adds the wrong person permanently attaches that guest: the wrong address receives the calendar invite and every subsequent update, and the only remediation is cancelling the entire booking.

[ADVISORY] Attendee rows are committed at line 92 before the unprotected updateCalendarAttendees call, so a calendar failure 500s the mutation after the DB write and the user's retry then hits the uniqueGuests.length === 0 path. Retrying a legitimately unique email list fails with the misleading BAD_REQUEST 'emails_must_be_unique_valid' (the guests are now existing attendees), the calendar event never gains the guests, and the organizer is left with no working path to complete the operation.

[ADVISORY] MultiEmail gets a code-splitting lazy wrapper justified by the copied comment 'These are like 40kb that not every user needs', but the component imports only Button, EmailField, Icon, and Tooltip — primitives already in the @calcom/ui main bundle. The next developer tracing the @calcom/ui MultiEmail export lands in a false-justification indirection and an extra async chunk boundary inside a dialog for a ~2KB component; deleting MultiEmailLazy and exporting MultiEmail directly removes a file and the false comment with it.

[BUG] The isTeamAdminOrOwner check joins isTeamAdmin and isTeamOwner with && instead of ||, and since isTeamAdmin already returns true for owners the conjunction collapses to owner-only, so the guard admits only team owners despite its name and stated intent. A team ADMIN (not owner) who opens the Add Guests dialog on a team booking is rejected with FORBIDDEN you_do_not_have_permission, making the feature silently unavailable to that entire role.

[BUG] sendAddGuestsEmails is called with the raw input `guests` instead of the filtered `uniqueGuests` that were actually persisted, so addresses deliberately excluded from creation are still classified as new guests by the email layer. An existing attendee whose email was re-submitted matches newGuests in email-manager.ts and receives a duplicate AttendeeScheduledEmail 'you are booked' confirmation instead of the AttendeeAddGuestsEmail 'guests added' notification.

[BUG] The EventManager is constructed from the calling user's identity and credentials (getUsersCredentials(ctx.user)) even though the calendar event being updated belongs to the booking's organizer, whose credentials the booking query explicitly fetched at lines 35-40 and then never used. When a team admin/owner or an attendee — exactly the roles the permission block admits — adds guests, updateCalendarAttendees finds no credential matching the organizer's destination calendar and silently skips the update: guests are emailed but never added to the actual Google/Outlook calendar event.

[BUG] The duplicate filter compares guest input to stored attendee emails with case-sensitive === even though email identity is case-insensitive, so a case-variant of an existing attendee passes as unique. Submitting 'John@Corp.com' when 'john@corp.com' is already an attendee reaches createMany and breaks the booking's attendee-email identity — an unhandled Prisma P2002 surfaces as a raw 500 toast where the (bookingId,email) unique constraint exists, and duplicate attendee rows that receive every subsequent booking email twice where it does not.

[BUG] The server-side schema omits the uniqueness refinement its client-side copy (AddGuestsDialog.tsx lines 26-29) enforces, and the handler never dedupes within the guests array, so the two validation copies already disagree and the API accepts ['a@x.com','a@x.com']. A direct mutation with in-request duplicates — or two concurrent requests adding the same address, since the check-then-insert at handler lines 74-81 is backed by no unique-index enforcement in this flow — hits createMany and produces a raw Prisma P2002 shown to the user as an untranslated INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR toast, or duplicate attendee rows when no constraint exists.

[BUG] The handler guards only booking existence and caller permission and never checks booking.status, so guests can be added to CANCELLED and REJECTED bookings. Adding guests to a cancelled booking persists attendee rows and sends new guests a full AttendeeScheduledEmail with a CONFIRMED-status ICS for an event that no longer exists, while updateCalendarAttendees attempts to update a calendar event that was deleted with the booking.

[BUG] Attendee rows are committed at the prisma.booking.update before the calendar update and email send run, with no compensation, and the duplicate filter subsequently treats those persisted guests as already-existing attendees. When updateCalendarAttendees throws (e.g. an expired calendar token), the mutation returns an error with the guests already stored but never emailed or calendar-added, and the user's retry is rejected with BAD_REQUEST emails_must_be_unique_valid — the operation can never be completed.

[BUG] The organizer lookup runs findFirstOrThrow on the sentinel id `booking.userId || 0`, which throws an unhandled Prisma P2025 for any booking whose nullable userId is null — a case the code itself anticipates by writing || 0. A caller admitted through the attendee or team-owner path on a userId-null booking receives a 500 Internal Server Error instead of the guests being added.

[BUG] The team-member notification loop in sendAddGuestsEmails can never execute because its only caller, addGuestsHandler, constructs evt without a `team` property, leaving calendarEvent.team?.members undefined (formatCalEvent does not add one). On team and collective bookings, team members other than the organizer never receive the OrganizerAddGuestsEmail this branch was written to send — the notification design silently degrades to organizer-only.

[ADVISORY] The guests array carries no .max() bound and the handler enforces no request-size limit, so a single authenticated mutation accepts an arbitrarily large guest list. Any permitted caller — including a mere attendee of any booking — can submit thousands of emails in one request, creating thousands of attendee rows and triggering a matching sendAddGuestsEmails blast, with nothing server-side to throttle it.

[ADVISORY] The handler reads seatsPerTimeSlot into evt but enforces no capacity invariant before createMany, so guest additions are not bounded by remaining seats. On a fully-booked seat-based event type, the organizer can push attendee rows past seatsPerTimeSlot, overbooking the slot with no error and corrupting seat-count displays.

[ADVISORY] Guests are persisted with name:"" and the organizer's timeZone and locale, so the attendee record asserts values the guest never provided. Every downstream email addresses the guest as ' <email>' with a blank display name and blank greeting, and ICS rendering uses the organizer's timezone for the guest.

[ADVISORY] The remove-button tooltip hardcodes the English literal "Remove email" while the rest of the component localizes every user-facing string through t(). Non-English users see an untranslated English tooltip inside an otherwise localized dialog.

[BUG] isInvalidEmail is set to true on failed validation but is never reset on successful validation or on mutation success — only the Cancel button clears it. After one invalid attempt, the 'Emails must be unique and valid' error banner persists through a successful add and reappears when the user reopens the dialog over a fresh empty form.

[BUG] isTeamAdminOrOwner combines isTeamAdmin and isTeamOwner with && although the variable name and the surrounding FORBIDDEN gate express an admin-OR-owner permission model, silently narrowing the accepted access rule to owners only. A team ADMIN who is not the team owner opens a teammate's booking and clicks additional_guests; isTeamAdminOrOwner evaluates false and the handler throws FORBIDDEN you_do_not_have_permission, so an entire role loses the guest-management feature this PR claims to deliver — the access-control objective was changed without any acceptance.

[BUG] The server schema accepts duplicate emails within guests (no uniqueness refine), while the client hand-copies the schema inline in AddGuestsDialog.tsx:26-29 with a uniqueness refine, so the accepted 'emails must be unique' constraint is enforced only in the UI and the two hand-maintained copies have already drifted. A direct addGuests mutation with guests ["a@b.com","a@b.com"] passes server validation; the handler's filter (addGuests.handler.ts:74-78) only dedupes against existing attendees, so both copies reach createMany and the guest ends up duplicated in the attendee list receiving duplicate invitation emails and a duplicated ICS attendee entry, or the insert dies with a raw Prisma unique-constraint 500.

[BUG] The catch block around sendAddGuestsEmails discards the caught err and logs only the static string 'Error sending AddGuestsEmails', then the handler returns success. When the email send fails, the organizer still sees the 'Guests added' success toast while no attendee was notified, and operations has no error message or stack trace in the logs to diagnose the delivery failure.

[BUG] The mutation's onSuccess resets multiEmailValue but never resets isInvalidEmail, so the validation-error banner survives a successful submission. A user who triggers the 'Emails must be unique and valid' banner, corrects the address, and adds guests successfully sees the same red error banner immediately upon reopening the dialog for the next booking, over a fresh empty form.

[BUG] sendAddGuestsEmails is called with the raw guests input instead of the filtered uniqueGuests array, so the email layer's newGuests classification includes emails the handler explicitly refused to add. When a user submits an existing attendee's email alongside new guests, that existing attendee matches newGuests.includes() in email-manager.ts:541 and receives a duplicate AttendeeScheduledEmail booking confirmation instead of the AttendeeAddGuestsEmail 'guests added' notice.

[BUG] The organizer lookup runs findFirstOrThrow on booking.userId || 0, so a booking with a null userId (a case the code itself anticipates) queries user id 0 and throws an unhandled Prisma P2025. An attendee of an unassigned team booking who adds guests passes the permission gate and then receives a 500 INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR from the crashed findFirstOrThrow instead of a 4xx response.

[BUG] The booking query filters only on id with no status constraint, so the addGuests mutation accepts cancelled and rejected bookings. Adding guests to a cancelled booking creates attendee rows, calls updateCalendarAttendees on the organizer's calendar event for a meeting that will never happen, and emails the new guest a CONFIRMED ICS invitation to a dead event.

[BUG] The duplicate check compares guest === attendee.email case-sensitively while the blacklist check on the very next line lowercases both sides, so the same address in different casing bypasses dedup. Re-adding an attendee as John@Example.com when the stored row is john@example.com creates a second BookingAttendee row for the same person, who then receives both the scheduled confirmation and the guests-added email.

[ADVISORY] The team-member notification loop in sendAddGuestsEmails is dead code for this feature because the only caller (addGuests.handler.ts:124-147) builds evt without a team field, so calendarEvent.team is always undefined. Non-organizer team members of collective/round-robin bookings never receive the 'Guests added' notification this loop was written to send, and the next maintainer assumes team notification works because the branch exists; either populate evt.team in the handler or delete the loop.

[ADVISORY] The handler persists the new attendees (lines 92-105) before updateCalendarAttendees with no compensation, so a calendar-API failure leaves the database mutated while the mutation returns an error. When the calendar provider rejects the update, the guests are already stored; the organizer retries and now gets BAD_REQUEST 'emails_must_be_unique_valid' because the guests are existing attendees, leaving a half-applied state with a misleading error and no calendar update.

[ADVISORY] The EventManager is constructed from the caller's credentials (getUsersCredentials(ctx.user)) even though the booking query includes booking.user.credentials, which then goes unused, so the calendar update runs as whoever called the mutation rather than the booking's organizer. When a non-organizer (an attendee or team admin, both explicitly allowed by the permission gate) adds guests, updateCalendarAttendees runs with no credential for the organizer's destination calendar, so the organizer's external calendar event is left without the new guests while the confirmation emails claim they were added; the included-but-unused credentials in the query show the original intent was to use the organizer's.

[BUG] The BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS deny list is lowercased (line 71) but each guest email is compared against it without lowercasing (line 77), so the operator-configured blacklist is bypassed by any case variation. An organizer or attendee adds a blacklisted address simply by capitalizing one character (e.g. ATTACKER@evil.com against the blacklist entry attacker@evil.com, which zod's .email() accepts unchanged); the address is created as an attendee and receives the full booking details including location and the video meeting URL/password, defeating the deny-list control.

[BUG] The permission check named isTeamAdminOrOwner joins isTeamAdmin and isTeamOwner with && instead of ||, requiring the caller to be both admin and owner of the booking's team. Team admins who are not owners (and owners who are not admins) are wrongly rejected with FORBIDDEN when adding guests to team bookings, so the authorization control does not implement its own stated admin-or-owner semantics and the feature silently fails for the entire admin role.

[BUG] The uniqueGuests filter only removes emails that match pre-existing attendees, and the server-side ZAddGuestsInputSchema (addGuests.schema.ts:5) omits the uniqueness refine the client applies in AddGuestsDialog.tsx, so duplicate emails within a single request each create an attendee row. A direct tRPC call with guests:["victim@x.com","victim@x.com",...] bypasses the dialog's client-only refine, creates N duplicate attendee rows for the same mailbox, and sendAddGuestsEmails then sends one full-details email per duplicate row — a single mutation becomes an N-email bomb to a chosen address and permanently corrupts the booking's attendee list.

[BUG] ZAddGuestsInputSchema places no maximum length on the guests array, so the mutation accepts an arbitrarily large list of emails in one call. Any attendee of any booking — the weakest authorization tier this endpoint grants — submits a 10,000-entry guests array, creating 10,000 attendee rows and triggering 10,000+ full-detail emails (one per new guest plus one per existing attendee) with no server-side cap, an email-bombing and resource-exhaustion vector through the platform's mail infrastructure.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] ZAddGuestsInputSchema validates email format but drops the uniqueness requirement that the client-side refine in AddGuestsDialog.tsx:26-29 enforces, leaving the directly callable tRPC mutation without it. adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The dedup/blacklist filter compares emails case-sensitively (guest === attendee.email and blacklistedGuestEmails.includes(guest)) while the blacklist is lowercased and guest input is never normalized. A booker whose attendee record was stored with different letter-casing than their login email (e.g. typed John@Mail.com into the booking form) is wrongfully FORBIDDEN from adding guests to their own booking.

adjudication.rationale: In the new `addGuestsHandler` the permission check `const isAttendee = !!booking.attendees.find((attendee) => attendee.email === user.email);` compares emails with strict, case-sensitive equality. adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, the server computes `uniqueGuests` by filtering out emails already in `booking.attendees`, but then calls `sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests)` with the *raw* input array `guests` (not `uniqueGuests`). adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] When booking.userId is null the organizer lookup runs findFirstOrThrow({ id: booking.userId || 0 }), which throws a raw Prisma P2025 not-found error that no TRPCError wraps. adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, the organizer is fetched with `prisma.user.findFirstOrThrow({ where: { id: booking.userId || 0 } })`. If `booking.userId` is `null`, this queries `id = 0` and `findFirstOrThrow` will throw a Prisma not-found error (e.g., P2025). adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] ZAddGuestsInputSchema puts no upper bound on the guests array and the handler applies no count limit. adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The handler fetches the booking by id alone and never checks booking.status, so addGuests accepts CANCELLED and REJECTED bookings. adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The guests array has no .max() bound and the handler performs no volume check, while the permission model deliberately lets any booking attendee invoke the mutation. An authenticated attendee submits thousands of emails in one request and the handler creates an attendee row and dispatches a scheduled email for each plus a notification to every existing attendee, turning the organizer's booking into an unbounded spam amplifier with no count or rate limit anywhere on the path.

The handler will create rows for each (`attendees.createMany`) and `sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests)` will send emails to organizer/team members plus one email per attendee in `calendarEvent.attendees` (including newly added guests and existing attendees), making this a potential unbounded spam amplifier path as described.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The handler reads seatsPerTimeSlot into evt at line 145 but never enforces it before createMany, so guest additions bypass the seat-capacity invariant that the normal booking flow enforces. For a fully-booked seats event type, an organizer or attendee adds any number of guests and the handler inserts attendee rows past seatsPerTimeSlot, overbooking the seat-limited event that the seats feature exists to cap.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The diff ships 174 lines of permission, filtering, and mutation logic plus a new dialog and a new shared UI component with zero tests. adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The isTeamAdminOrOwner check joins isTeamAdmin and isTeamOwner with && instead of ||, and since isTeamAdmin already returns true for owners the conjunction collapses to owner-only, so the guard admits only team owners despite its name and stated intent. adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] sendAddGuestsEmails is called with the raw input `guests` instead of the filtered `uniqueGuests` that were actually persisted, so addresses deliberately excluded from creation are still classified as new guests by the email layer. An existing attendee whose email was re-submitted matches newGuests in email-manager.ts and receives a duplicate AttendeeScheduledEmail 'you are booked' confirmation instead of the AttendeeAddGuestsEmail 'guests added' notification.

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, the server filters the requested emails into `uniqueGuests` (excluding existing attendees and blacklisted addresses) and only persists `uniqueGuests` via `createMany`. However, it later calls `sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests)` using the raw input `guests` instead of `uniqueGuests`. In `email-manager.ts`, `sendAddGuestsEmails` uses the passed `newGuests` list to decide per-attendee email type: `if (newGuests.includes(attendee.email))` it sends `AttendeeScheduledEmail`, otherwise `AttendeeAddGuestsEmail`. Therefore, if a user re-submits an existing attendee email (filtered out from persistence), that existing attendee is still treated as a “new guest” by the email layer and can receive a duplicate scheduled/confirmation email. Same issue applies to blacklisted emails being treated as new for classification.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The EventManager is constructed from the calling user's identity and credentials (getUsersCredentials(ctx.user)) even though the calendar event being updated belongs to the booking's organizer, whose credentials the booking query explicitly fetched at lines 35-40 and then never used. When a team admin/owner or an attendee — exactly the roles the permission block admits — adds guests, updateCalendarAttendees finds no credential matching the organizer's destination calendar and silently skips the update: guests are emailed but never added to the actual Google/Outlook calendar event.

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, the calendar update is performed via `new EventManager({ ...user, credentials: [...credentials] })` where `user`/`credentials` come from `ctx.user` (`getUsersCredentials(ctx.user)`). However, the booking being updated belongs to `booking.userId` (the organizer), and the booking query explicitly includes `user.credentials`/`user.destinationCalendar` but those are never used. Since the permission check allows non-organizers (attendees, and potentially team roles), this can construct an EventManager with credentials that don't correspond to the organizer’s connected calendar, causing `updateCalendarAttendees(evt, booking)` to fail/skip while the DB update + emails still proceed.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The duplicate filter compares guest input to stored attendee emails with case-sensitive === even though email identity is case-insensitive, so a case-variant of an existing attendee passes as unique. Submitting 'John@Corp.com' when 'john@corp.com' is already an attendee reaches createMany and breaks the booking's attendee-email identity — an unhandled Prisma P2002 surfaces as a raw 500 toast where the (bookingId,email) unique constraint exists, and duplicate attendee rows that receive every subsequent booking email twice where it does not.

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, the dedupe check uses a case-sensitive comparison: `guest === attendee.email` inside `uniqueGuests` filtering. Because emails are generally treated as case-insensitive identifiers, a case-variant like `John@Corp.com` will not be filtered out when `john@corp.com` already exists, allowing a logical duplicate to proceed into `attendees.createMany`. The code also lowercases the blacklist entries but compares them to `guest` without lowercasing, so case-variants can bypass the blacklist as well. The later behavior about Prisma `P2002`/DB uniqueness is not shown in the diff, but the case-sensitive dedupe itself is a concrete correctness issue introduced here.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The server-side schema omits the uniqueness refinement its client-side copy (AddGuestsDialog.tsx lines 26-29) enforces, and the handler never dedupes within the guests array, so the two validation copies already disagree and the API accepts ['a@x.com','a@x.com']. A direct mutation with in-request duplicates — or two concurrent requests adding the same address, since the check-then-insert at handler lines 74-81 is backed by no unique-index enforcement in this flow — hits createMany and produces a raw Prisma P2002 shown to the user as an untranslated INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR toast, or duplicate attendee rows when no constraint exists.

adjudication.rationale: The client-side dialog defines a local ZAddGuestsInputSchema with a uniqueness `refine` (AddGuestsDialog.tsx) but the server-side ZAddGuestsInputSchema (addGuests.schema.ts) only validates `z.array(z.string().email())` with no uniqueness constraint. In the handler, `uniqueGuests` only filters against existing `booking.attendees` and blacklist (addGuests.handler.ts), and does not dedupe duplicates within the incoming `guests` array, so `['a@x.com','a@x.com']` can pass server validation and reach `createMany`. Whether this results in duplicate attendee rows or a DB constraint error depends on schema constraints not shown here, but the API accepting in-request duplicates and the client/server validation mismatch are directly verifiable from the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The handler guards only booking existence and caller permission and never checks booking.status, so guests can be added to CANCELLED and REJECTED bookings. Adding guests to a cancelled booking persists attendee rows and sends new guests a full AttendeeScheduledEmail with a CONFIRMED-status ICS for an event that no longer exists, while updateCalendarAttendees attempts to update a calendar event that was deleted with the booking.

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, the booking lookup only filters by `id` and then checks caller role/permission (`isTeamAdminOrOwner`/`isOrganizer`/`isAttendee`). There is no conditional guarding against booking lifecycle state before mutating data (`prisma.booking.update(... attendees.createMany ...)`) and triggering side effects (`eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees(evt, booking)` and `sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests)`). As written, the mutation will run for any booking record that exists and passes permission checks, so if cancelled/rejected bookings are still present in the DB, guests can be added and emails/calendar updates attempted for them.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] Attendee rows are committed at the prisma.booking.update before the calendar update and email send run, with no compensation, and the duplicate filter subsequently treats those persisted guests as already-existing attendees. When updateCalendarAttendees throws (e.g. an expired calendar token), the mutation returns an error with the guests already stored but never emailed or calendar-added, and the user's retry is rejected with BAD_REQUEST emails_must_be_unique_valid — the operation can never be completed.

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, the mutation persists new attendees via `prisma.booking.update({ data: { attendees: { createMany: ... }}})` before calling `eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees(evt, booking)` and before sending emails. There is no transaction/rollback/compensation. If `updateCalendarAttendees` throws, the handler will error out (not caught), leaving guests stored in DB but without calendar sync and without emails. On retry, `uniqueGuests` is computed by filtering out emails already present in `booking.attendees`, which will now include the previously-persisted guests, making `uniqueGuests.length === 0` and causing `BAD_REQUEST` (`emails_must_be_unique_valid`). This matches the finding: a partial write makes the operation non-retriable and permanently incomplete.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The organizer lookup runs findFirstOrThrow on the sentinel id `booking.userId || 0`, which throws an unhandled Prisma P2025 for any booking whose nullable userId is null — a case the code itself anticipates by writing || 0. A caller admitted through the attendee or team-owner path on a userId-null booking receives a 500 Internal Server Error instead of the guests being added.

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, the organizer is fetched via `prisma.user.findFirstOrThrow({ where: { id: booking.userId || 0 } })`. Since `booking.userId` is treated as nullable elsewhere (`booking.userId || 0`), a null `userId` will cause an `id: 0` lookup and `findFirstOrThrow` will throw (Prisma P2025) with no surrounding catch. The earlier permission gate allows access via `isAttendee` (based on `booking.attendees`) or the team-admin/owner path even when `booking.userId` is null, so this can surface as a 500 instead of adding guests.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The team-member notification loop in sendAddGuestsEmails can never execute because its only caller, addGuestsHandler, constructs evt without a `team` property, leaving calendarEvent.team?.members undefined (formatCalEvent does not add one). On team and collective bookings, team members other than the organizer never receive the OrganizerAddGuestsEmail this branch was written to send — the notification design silently degrades to organizer-only.

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuestsHandler`, the `CalendarEvent` (`evt`) passed to `sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests)` is constructed without any `team` field (only `title/type/description/times/organizer/attendees/...`). In `sendAddGuestsEmails`, the only way to notify additional team members is the branch `if (calendarEvent.team?.members) { for (const teamMember of calendarEvent.team.members) ... }`, which will be skipped when `team` is undefined. The diff also shows the booking query includes `eventType: true` but does not include `eventType.team`/`team.members`, so there is no source in this handler to populate `evt.team`. adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The guests array carries no .max() bound and the handler enforces no request-size limit, so a single authenticated mutation accepts an arbitrarily large guest list. Any permitted caller — including a mere attendee of any booking — can submit thousands of emails in one request, creating thousands of attendee rows and triggering a matching sendAddGuestsEmails blast, with nothing server-side to throttle it.

adjudication.rationale: The new mutation input schema `ZAddGuestsInputSchema` defines `guests: z.array(z.string().email())` with no `.max()` (packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.schema.ts), and the handler performs `attendees.createMany` with the provided list (addGuests.handler.ts) and then calls `sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests)` which maps over `calendarEvent.attendees` to send emails (packages/emails/email-manager.ts). The authorization explicitly allows any attendee (`isAttendee`) to call the mutation, not just the organizer/admin. As a result, a permitted caller can submit an arbitrarily large guests array, creating many DB rows and triggering a large outbound email burst with no server-side throttling/limit shown in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The handler reads seatsPerTimeSlot into evt but enforces no capacity invariant before createMany, so guest additions are not bounded by remaining seats. On a fully-booked seat-based event type, the organizer can push attendee rows past seatsPerTimeSlot, overbooking the slot with no error and corrupting seat-count displays.

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuestsHandler` the code unconditionally appends new attendee rows via `prisma.booking.update({ data: { attendees: { createMany: ... }}})` without checking `booking.eventType?.seatsPerTimeSlot` (or any remaining-capacity invariant) before inserting. Although `seatsPerTimeSlot` is copied into `evt`, it is never used to block additions. For seat-based event types, this allows adding guests beyond capacity, creating an overbooked booking and potentially breaking seat-count/attendee displays.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] Guests are persisted with name:"" and the organizer's timeZone and locale, so the attendee record asserts values the guest never provided. Every downstream email addresses the guest as ' <email>' with a blank display name and blank greeting, and ICS rendering uses the organizer's timezone for the guest.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] isTeamAdminOrOwner combines isTeamAdmin and isTeamOwner with && although the variable name and the surrounding FORBIDDEN gate express an admin-OR-owner permission model, silently narrowing the accepted access rule to owners only. A team ADMIN who is not the team owner opens a teammate's booking and clicks additional_guests; isTeamAdminOrOwner evaluates false and the handler throws FORBIDDEN you_do_not_have_permission, so an entire role loses the guest-management feature this PR claims to deliver — the access-control objective was changed without any acceptance.

In `addGuests.handler.ts`, `isTeamAdminOrOwner` is computed with `&&`:

But the name and the subsequent permission gate (`if (!isTeamAdminOrOwner && !isOrganizer && !isAttendee) throw FORBIDDEN`) imply an admin-OR-owner rule. A direct addGuests mutation with guests ["a@b.com","a@b.com"] passes server validation; the handler's filter (addGuests.handler.ts:74-78) only dedupes against existing attendees, so both copies reach createMany and the guest ends up duplicated in the attendee list receiving duplicate invitation emails and a duplicated ICS attendee entry, or the insert dies with a raw Prisma unique-constraint 500.
