adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The catch block around sendAddGuestsEmails discards the caught err and logs only the static string 'Error sending AddGuestsEmails', then the handler returns success. When the email send fails, the organizer still sees the 'Guests added' success toast while no attendee was notified, and operations has no error message or stack trace in the logs to diagnose the delivery failure.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts`, the email send is wrapped in `try { await sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests); } catch (err) { console.log("Error sending AddGuestsEmails"); }`, which swallows `err` and logs only a static message, then the handler still returns `{ message: "Guests added" }`. This is verifiably poor observability and can hide delivery failures, but it doesn’t break the core mutation outcome shown in the diff (guests are still added to the booking and calendars are updated), and the UI toast `t("guests_added")` reflects the mutation success rather than explicitly guaranteeing email delivery.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The mutation's onSuccess resets multiEmailValue but never resets isInvalidEmail, so the validation-error banner survives a successful submission. A user who triggers the 'Emails must be unique and valid' banner, corrects the address, and adds guests successfully sees the same red error banner immediately upon reopening the dialog for the next booking, over a fresh empty form.

adjudication.rationale: In `AddGuestsDialog`, `isInvalidEmail` is set to `true` on validation failure (`setIsInvalidEmail(true)` in `handleAdd`), but the mutation `onSuccess` only closes the dialog and resets `multiEmailValue` (`setMultiEmailValue([""])`) and never calls `setIsInvalidEmail(false)`. Since the dialog component remains mounted (rendered unconditionally in `BookingListItem`), reopening it after a successful submission can still show the red validation banner (`{isInvalidEmail && ...}`) despite a fresh/cleared input.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] sendAddGuestsEmails is called with the raw guests input instead of the filtered uniqueGuests array, so the email layer's newGuests classification includes emails the handler explicitly refused to add. When a user submits an existing attendee's email alongside new guests, that existing attendee matches newGuests.includes() in email-manager.ts:541 and receives a duplicate AttendeeScheduledEmail booking confirmation instead of the AttendeeAddGuestsEmail 'guests added' notice.

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, the handler computes `uniqueGuests` by filtering out emails already in `booking.attendees` and blacklisted emails, and only creates attendees from `uniqueGuests`. However it calls `sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests)` with the raw input array `guests` (not `uniqueGuests`). In `email-manager.ts`, `sendAddGuestsEmails` uses `newGuests.includes(attendee.email)` to decide whether to send `AttendeeScheduledEmail` vs `AttendeeAddGuestsEmail`. If the raw input includes an existing attendee email alongside new guests, that existing attendee will match `includes(...)` and receive an extra `AttendeeScheduledEmail` even though they were not newly added—exactly the misclassification described.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The organizer lookup runs findFirstOrThrow on booking.userId || 0, so a booking with a null userId (a case the code itself anticipates) queries user id 0 and throws an unhandled Prisma P2025. An attendee of an unassigned team booking who adds guests passes the permission gate and then receives a 500 INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR from the crashed findFirstOrThrow instead of a 4xx response.

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, the organizer is fetched with `prisma.user.findFirstOrThrow({ where: { id: booking.userId || 0 } })`. If `booking.userId` is `null`/`undefined` (which the code explicitly anticipates via `|| 0`), this queries `id: 0` and `findFirstOrThrow` will throw when no user exists. That exception is not caught (only email sending is wrapped in `try/catch`), so the mutation can fail with a 500 instead of returning a controlled 4xx/handled error. The permission gate can still allow an attendee (`isAttendee`) through even when `booking.userId` is null, making this reachable.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The booking query filters only on id with no status constraint, so the addGuests mutation accepts cancelled and rejected bookings. Adding guests to a cancelled booking creates attendee rows, calls updateCalendarAttendees on the organizer's calendar event for a meeting that will never happen, and emails the new guest a CONFIRMED ICS invitation to a dead event.

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuestsHandler`, the booking is loaded with `prisma.booking.findFirst({ where: { id: bookingId } ... })` and there is no subsequent guard on booking state (e.g., cancelled/rejected) before it (1) creates attendee rows via `prisma.booking.update(... attendees.createMany ...)`, (2) calls `eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees(evt, booking)`, and (3) sends emails via `sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests)`. Since the code applies to any booking id the user is authorized for, it would also apply to non-active bookings if such statuses exist, leading to calendar/email side effects for an event that should be considered inactive.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The duplicate check compares guest === attendee.email case-sensitively while the blacklist check on the very next line lowercases both sides, so the same address in different casing bypasses dedup. Re-adding an attendee as John@Example.com when the stored row is john@example.com creates a second BookingAttendee row for the same person, who then receives both the scheduled confirmation and the guests-added email.

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, `uniqueGuests` filters out existing attendees with a case-sensitive check: `!booking.attendees.some((attendee) => guest === attendee.email)`. This allows `John@Example.com` to be added even if `john@example.com` already exists, creating a duplicate `BookingAttendee` row. Since `sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests)` uses `newGuests.includes(attendee.email)` to decide which template to send, the two differently-cased emails can cause the same mailbox to receive multiple notifications. (Also, the blacklist check is not normalized either: `blacklistedGuestEmails` is lowercased but `guest` is not.)

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The team-member notification loop in sendAddGuestsEmails is dead code for this feature because the only caller (addGuests.handler.ts:124-147) builds evt without a team field, so calendarEvent.team is always undefined. Non-organizer team members of collective/round-robin bookings never receive the 'Guests added' notification this loop was written to send, and the next maintainer assumes team notification works because the branch exists; either populate evt.team in the handler or delete the loop.

adjudication.rationale: In addGuests.handler.ts the CalendarEvent `evt` passed to `sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests)` is constructed without a `team` field (it sets organizer, attendees, destinationCalendar, etc., but never `team`). In email-manager.ts, `sendAddGuestsEmails` only notifies additional organizer recipients via `if (calendarEvent.team?.members) { ... }`, so on this code path that branch is never taken and non-organizer team members will not receive the "Guests added" email despite the presence of that loop. The claim that this is the only caller cannot be proven from the diff, but the dead-branch behavior for this caller is directly verifiable.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The handler persists the new attendees (lines 92-105) before updateCalendarAttendees with no compensation, so a calendar-API failure leaves the database mutated while the mutation returns an error. When the calendar provider rejects the update, the guests are already stored; the organizer retries and now gets BAD_REQUEST 'emails_must_be_unique_valid' because the guests are existing attendees, leaving a half-applied state with a misleading error and no calendar update.

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuestsHandler`, the DB is updated first via `prisma.booking.update(... attendees.createMany ...)` (lines ~92-105), and only afterwards it calls `await eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees(evt, booking);` (near the end). There is no transaction/rollback or compensation if `updateCalendarAttendees` throws, so a calendar-provider failure will leave the booking’s attendees persisted while the mutation errors. On retry, `uniqueGuests` is computed against the original `booking.attendees` loaded before the update, but the next run will load the now-updated attendees and `uniqueGuests.length === 0` will trigger `TRPCError(BAD_REQUEST, "emails_must_be_unique_valid")`, matching the described half-applied state and misleading error.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The EventManager is constructed from the caller's credentials (getUsersCredentials(ctx.user)) even though the booking query includes booking.user.credentials, which then goes unused, so the calendar update runs as whoever called the mutation rather than the booking's organizer. When a non-organizer (an attendee or team admin, both explicitly allowed by the permission gate) adds guests, updateCalendarAttendees runs with no credential for the organizer's destination calendar, so the organizer's external calendar event is left without the new guests while the confirmation emails claim they were added; the included-but-unused credentials in the query show the original intent was to use the organizer's.

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, the booking is fetched with `user: { include: { destinationCalendar: true, credentials: true } }` but those organizer credentials are never used. Instead, `credentials` are obtained via `getUsersCredentials(ctx.user)` and `EventManager` is constructed with `...user` where `user` is the caller from `ctx` (who may be an attendee or team admin/owner per the permission checks). The subsequent `eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees(evt, booking)` therefore runs under the caller’s credentials rather than the booking organizer’s, which can prevent updating the organizer’s external calendar event while emails are still sent claiming guests were added.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS deny list is lowercased (line 71) but each guest email is compared against it without lowercasing (line 77), so the operator-configured blacklist is bypassed by any case variation. An organizer or attendee adds a blacklisted address simply by capitalizing one character (e.g. ATTACKER@evil.com against the blacklist entry attacker@evil.com, which zod's .email() accepts unchanged); the address is created as an attendee and receives the full booking details including location and the video meeting URL/password, defeating the deny-list control.
matched_golden_ids: The addGuests.handler.ts blacklist check uses blacklistedGuestEmails.includes(guest) after lowercasing the blacklist but not the input guest emails, allowing attackers to bypass BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS restrictions by submitting emails with uppercase characters.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: The candidate describes the same flaw: the blacklist is normalized to lowercase but guest emails are not, and the code uses an includes() comparison, allowing bypass via uppercase/case variations.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The permission check named isTeamAdminOrOwner joins isTeamAdmin and isTeamOwner with && instead of ||, requiring the caller to be both admin and owner of the booking's team. Team admins who are not owners (and owners who are not admins) are wrongly rejected with FORBIDDEN when adding guests to team bookings, so the authorization control does not implement its own stated admin-or-owner semantics and the feature silently fails for the entire admin role.

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, `isTeamAdminOrOwner` is computed with `&&` between `isTeamAdmin(...)` and `isTeamOwner(...)`, meaning the user must be both admin and owner to pass (`const isTeamAdminOrOwner = ... && ...`). This contradicts the variable name/intent (“admin or owner”) and will incorrectly reject team admins who aren’t owners (and vice versa) via the subsequent `FORBIDDEN` check (`if (!isTeamAdminOrOwner && !isOrganizer && !isAttendee) ...`).

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The uniqueGuests filter only removes emails that match pre-existing attendees, and the server-side ZAddGuestsInputSchema (addGuests.schema.ts:5) omits the uniqueness refine the client applies in AddGuestsDialog.tsx, so duplicate emails within a single request each create an attendee row. A direct tRPC call with guests:["victim@x.com","victim@x.com",...] bypasses the dialog's client-only refine, creates N duplicate attendee rows for the same mailbox, and sendAddGuestsEmails then sends one full-details email per duplicate row — a single mutation becomes an N-email bomb to a chosen address and permanently corrupts the booking's attendee list.

adjudication.rationale: Verified in diff: server-side ZAddGuestsInputSchema (packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.schema.ts) only validates `guests` as `z.array(z.string().email())` with no uniqueness constraint, while the client dialog applies a uniqueness refine locally. In addGuests.handler.ts, `uniqueGuests` only filters out emails already in `booking.attendees` / blacklist, and does not dedupe duplicates within the incoming `guests` array, so a direct tRPC call with repeated emails will pass `uniqueGuests` and be forwarded to `attendees.createMany` as duplicate rows. After update, the code builds `attendeesList` from `bookingAttendees.attendees` and `sendAddGuestsEmails` iterates over `calendarEvent.attendees`, sending one email per attendee entry, so duplicates would multiply emails. (DB-level uniqueness constraints, if any, are not shown in the diff.)

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] ZAddGuestsInputSchema places no maximum length on the guests array, so the mutation accepts an arbitrarily large list of emails in one call. Any attendee of any booking — the weakest authorization tier this endpoint grants — submits a 10,000-entry guests array, creating 10,000 attendee rows and triggering 10,000+ full-detail emails (one per new guest plus one per existing attendee) with no server-side cap, an email-bombing and resource-exhaustion vector through the platform's mail infrastructure.

adjudication.rationale: The new TRPC input schema `ZAddGuestsInputSchema` (`packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.schema.ts`) allows `guests: z.array(z.string().email())` with no `.max(...)`/rate limiting visible in the diff. In `addGuests.handler.ts`, `uniqueGuests` is directly used in a `createMany` to insert all new attendees, and then `sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests)` triggers per-attendee emails via `calendarEvent.attendees.map(...)` in `sendAddGuestsEmails` with no cap. Since the endpoint explicitly permits any existing attendee (`isAttendee`) to call it, an attendee can submit a very large guests list and cause mass DB writes and mass outbound email sends (existing attendees + new guests + organizer/team), creating a resource-exhaustion / email-bombing vector.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The handler builds EventManager from the calling user's credentials (getUsersCredentials(ctx.user)) instead of the booking organizer's, while the booking.user.credentials rows fetched at line 38 are never used. When an attendee — a caller this endpoint explicitly authorizes — adds guests, updateCalendarAttendees runs with credentials that have no access to the organizer's calendar event, so the calendar attendee list is never updated (or the mutation throws after the DB write already persisted), and every request needlessly materializes the organizer's OAuth tokens in memory.

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, the endpoint explicitly authorizes non-organizers via `isAttendee` and then constructs `EventManager` with the *caller* identity/credentials: `const credentials = await getUsersCredentials(ctx.user); const eventManager = new EventManager({ ...user, credentials: [...credentials] });` and calls `eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees(evt, booking)`. The booking query earlier includes `user: { ... credentials: true }` (the organizer’s credentials) but those rows are never used. This makes it very likely that when an attendee (not the organizer) adds guests, the calendar update runs under credentials that don’t have access to the organizer’s calendar event, causing the external calendar update to fail/throw after the DB `booking.update(... createMany ...)` has already persisted. The unused inclusion also needlessly loads the organizer’s credential records into memory.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] sendAddGuestsEmails sends an email to every attendee on the booking on every invocation rather than only the newly added guests. An attendee (the lowest-privilege caller this endpoint authorizes) loops the addGuests mutation with one fresh guest per call and forces one 'Guests Added' email per call to the organizer and every other attendee — an unthrottled harassment/spam channel through the platform's mail sender that also degrades sending reputation.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/emails/email-manager.ts`, `sendAddGuestsEmails(calEvent, newGuests)` sends organizer/team emails every call and then unconditionally iterates `calendarEvent.attendees.map(...)` sending either `AttendeeScheduledEmail` or `AttendeeAddGuestsEmail` to *every* attendee, not just newly added ones. In `addGuests.handler.ts`, the endpoint authorizes any existing attendee (`isAttendee`) and has no throttling/rate limiting; repeated calls would repeatedly email the organizer and all attendees. This matches the finding’s spam/abuse vector grounded in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The existing-attendee dedup compares emails case-sensitively (guest === attendee.email) while guest emails are stored verbatim (line 86), so a case variant of an existing attendee is not filtered out. A caller re-adds alice@x.com as Alice@X.com, creating a second attendee row for the same real mailbox — the person is double-counted on the booking, receives duplicate emails, and appears twice on the calendar event.

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, existing-attendee de-dupe is `!booking.attendees.some((attendee) => guest === attendee.email)` and new attendee rows are created with `email: guest` (no normalization). Since neither side is lowercased/trimmed, `alice@x.com` vs `Alice@X.com` will bypass the filter and be inserted via `createMany`, leading to duplicate attendee rows/emails/calendar entries for the same mailbox. (Blacklist is lowercased but compared against unlowercased `guest` too.)

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] addGuests createMany's new attendees without ever checking booking.eventType.seatsPerTimeSlot, even though the handler is seats-aware (it copies seatsPerTimeSlot into evt at line 145). Organizers of seat-limited event types get bookings overbooked past the configured seat cap — the capacity limit enforced at booking time is bypassed through the guest-add path, so seats-based attendee counts and per-seat emails no longer match configured capacity.

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, the mutation unconditionally appends new `attendees` via `prisma.booking.update({ data: { attendees: { createMany: ... }}})` without checking any capacity constraint (e.g., `booking.eventType?.seatsPerTimeSlot`). Yet the handler explicitly includes `seatsPerTimeSlot`/`seatsShowAttendees` in the constructed `CalendarEvent` (`evt`), implying seat-limited/group events are in scope. If seats are enforced at booking time based on attendee count, this guest-add path can exceed the configured cap by adding more attendees after the booking is created.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] isTeamAdminOrOwner joins the two role checks with && instead of ||, so the caller must satisfy both isTeamAdmin and isTeamOwner for the team-permission branch to pass. A team ADMIN who is not the team owner is thrown FORBIDDEN ('you_do_not_have_permission') when adding guests to their team's booking — the exact role this check was written to allow is locked out, and the branch is effectively owner-only (or always false where roles are mutually exclusive).

adjudication.rationale:
In `packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts`, `isTeamAdminOrOwner` is computed with `&&`:
```ts
const isTeamAdminOrOwner =
  (await isTeamAdmin(user.id, booking.eventType?.teamId ?? 0)) &&
  (await isTeamOwner(user.id, booking.eventType?.teamId ?? 0));
```
This requires the caller to be both a team admin and the team owner to pass the team-permission branch. As a result, a user who is a team admin but not the owner will fail `isTeamAdminOrOwner` and can hit the `FORBIDDEN` path unless they’re also `isOrganizer` or `isAttendee`, matching the finding’s claim that admins are incorrectly locked out.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The catch around sendAddGuestsEmails discards the caught err and logs only the static string 'Error sending AddGuestsEmails', after which the handler returns { message: 'Guests added' }. When guest-notification email delivery fails, the user still sees the 'guests_added' success toast and the operator gets a log line with no error message or stack — the failure is undiagnosable and indistinguishable from success.

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, `sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests)` is wrapped in `try { ... } catch (err) { console.log("Error sending AddGuestsEmails"); }` which (a) discards `err` (no message/stack) and (b) does not propagate failure, so the mutation still resolves successfully and the UI `onSuccess` path shows the `guests_added` toast even if email sending failed. This makes a real failure mode (guest notification emails not sent) indistinguishable from success and hard to diagnose based on the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] uniqueGuests filters guests only against existing attendees and the blacklist, never against duplicates within the guests array, and the server-side ZAddGuestsInputSchema omits the uniqueness refine that the dialog's hand-copied client schema enforces. A direct addGuests mutation submitting the same email twice (['a@x.com','a@x.com']) passes server validation and reaches the attendees createMany, which throws an unhandled Prisma P2002 unique-constraint error — the caller gets HTTP 500 instead of the BAD_REQUEST the handler promises for invalid emails.

adjudication.rationale: The server-side input schema `ZAddGuestsInputSchema` (packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.schema.ts) only validates `guests` as `z.array(z.string().email())` and does not enforce uniqueness, unlike the dialog’s client-side `ZAddGuestsInputSchema` refine in `AddGuestsDialog.tsx`. In `addGuests.handler.ts`, `uniqueGuests` filters only against existing `booking.attendees` and the blacklist, but does not dedupe duplicates within the incoming `guests` array, so `guestsFullDetails` can contain the same email multiple times and is passed to `attendees.createMany`. The handler does not catch database errors around `prisma.booking.update`, so duplicate inserts can bubble up as an internal error rather than the intended `BAD_REQUEST` for invalid input.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The EventManager is constructed from the caller's credentials (getUsersCredentials(ctx.user), {...user}) even though the permission check explicitly authorizes attendees and team admins, while the organizer's credentials fetched via the booking query's user include (lines 35-39) are never used. When anyone other than the booking organizer invokes addGuests (e.g., a team admin on a round-robin booking), updateCalendarAttendees has no credential matching the organizer's destination calendar and silently skips the update — guests are persisted and emailed but never appear on the organizer's calendar event.

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, non-organizers (team admin/owner or attendee) are authorized to call the mutation, but the calendar update path constructs `EventManager` with the *caller* (`...user` from `ctx.user`) and `getUsersCredentials(ctx.user)`. The booking query includes `booking.user.credentials` (and destination calendar) but those organizer credentials are never used. Given `eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees(evt, booking)` relies on the `EventManager` instance’s credentials, a non-organizer caller may not have access to the organizer’s connected calendar, so the external calendar update can fail/skip while the DB attendees are still created and emails are sent.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] onSuccess resets multiEmailValue but never clears isInvalidEmail, and the AddGuestsDialog component stays mounted in BookingListItem between dialog opens. After a failed validation followed by a successful add (or after closing the dialog while the error banner is showing), reopening the dialog immediately displays the stale 'emails_must_be_unique_valid' error banner over a fresh empty form.

adjudication.rationale: In AddGuestsDialog, `isInvalidEmail` is set to `true` on failed validation in `handleAdd`, but it is only cleared in the Cancel button handler (`setIsInvalidEmail(false)`). In the mutation `onSuccess`, the dialog closes and `multiEmailValue` resets to `[""]`, but `isInvalidEmail` is never cleared. Since `BookingListItem` always renders `<AddGuestsDialog ... />` (it is not conditionally mounted), the dialog’s internal state persists between opens, so reopening can show the stale error banner over a fresh/empty form (also true when closing via `Dialog`'s `onOpenChange`).

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] sendAddGuestsEmails is passed the raw guests input instead of the uniqueGuests list that was actually persisted, so emails filtered out as already-on-the-booking still classify their owner as a new guest. A user who re-submits an existing attendee's email (the dialog cannot block this, it only checks format and intra-form uniqueness) causes that attendee to receive the full AttendeeScheduledEmail booking confirmation instead of the AttendeeAddGuestsEmail guests-added notification.

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, the server filters input `guests` into `uniqueGuests` (excluding emails already in `booking.attendees` and blacklisted) and persists only `uniqueGuests` via `createMany`. However it then calls `sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests)` with the raw, unfiltered input. In `email-manager.ts`, `sendAddGuestsEmails(calEvent, newGuests)` uses `newGuests.includes(attendee.email)` to decide which template to send, so any existing attendee whose email was re-submitted (not newly persisted) will match and receive the "new guest" path (`AttendeeScheduledEmail`) instead of the guests-added notification (`AttendeeAddGuestsEmail`). The UI validation only enforces email format and uniqueness within the form, not against existing attendees, so this is a real behavioral defect exposed by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] Guest deduplication compares emails case-sensitively (guest === attendee.email) even though email addresses are case-insensitive and no lowercasing is applied to the submitted guest. Submitting 'John@X.com' when 'john@x.com' is already an attendee passes the filter and creates a second attendee row differing only in case — the guest receives duplicate emails and appears twice on the calendar and in the ICS invite.

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, deduplication uses a case-sensitive comparison (`guest === attendee.email`) and does not normalize either side (no `toLowerCase()` on `guests` or existing `attendee.email`). This allows adding the same address with different casing (e.g., `John@X.com` vs `john@x.com`), creating duplicate attendee rows and triggering duplicate downstream effects (calendar/ICS + emails). The UI-side Zod refine in `AddGuestsDialog.tsx` also uses raw strings/`Set`, so it won’t catch case-variants either.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] addGuests performs three non-transactional side effects in sequence — attendee createMany (92-106), calendar update (165), emails (168) — with no compensation or rollback on failure. A failure in updateCalendarAttendees 500s the request after attendees are already persisted; the user's retry with the same valid emails then hits the uniqueGuests.length === 0 BAD_REQUEST 'emails_must_be_unique_valid' (lines 80-81), reporting their valid input as invalid, and nobody can tell the calendar was never updated.

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, the handler persists new attendees first via `prisma.booking.update(... attendees.createMany ...)` (lines ~92-106), then calls `eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees(evt, booking)` (line ~165) without a try/catch or transaction. If `updateCalendarAttendees` throws, the request errors after DB state has been mutated. On retry with the same emails, `uniqueGuests` is computed by filtering out already-existing attendees (`!booking.attendees.some(...)`), so it becomes empty and triggers `BAD_REQUEST` with message `emails_must_be_unique_valid` (lines ~80-81), even though the input emails are valid—exactly the inconsistent/irrecoverable state described. Emails are also sent after that (line ~168) with only email sending wrapped in try/catch, so no rollback occurs for earlier side effects.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The organizer lookup uses findFirstOrThrow({ where: { id: booking.userId || 0 } }), so a booking whose nullable userId is null resolves the query to id 0 and takes the throw path. An attendee of a null-userId booking who passes the permission check receives an unhandled Prisma P2025 error — HTTP 500 with no TRPCError shape — instead of any meaningful response.

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, the organizer is loaded via `prisma.user.findFirstOrThrow({ where: { id: booking.userId || 0 } })`. The use of `booking.userId || 0` implies `booking.userId` can be null/undefined; in that case it queries `id: 0` and `findFirstOrThrow` will throw a Prisma error (likely P2025). Since this is not wrapped/translated into a `TRPCError`, a caller who passes the permission gate via `isAttendee` (based on `booking.attendees`) could trigger an internal error rather than a meaningful TRPC error response.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] isTeamAdminOrOwner joins the two role checks with `&&`, requiring the caller to be simultaneously team admin AND team owner, contradicting the variable's name and the OR-shaped permission line that consumes it. A team ADMIN who is not the owner fails isTeamOwner, so the conjunction is false and they receive FORBIDDEN when adding guests to a team booking they don't organize — the branch grants nothing beyond the organizer/attendee paths, so the admin-or-owner permission it advertises is dead code.

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, `isTeamAdminOrOwner` is computed as `(await isTeamAdmin(...)) && (await isTeamOwner(...))`, which requires the user to be both a team admin and the team owner. The permission gate then uses `if (!isTeamAdminOrOwner && !isOrganizer && !isAttendee) throw FORBIDDEN;`, so a team admin who is not the owner (and not organizer/attendee) will be incorrectly forbidden. This contradicts the variable name and the intended “admin OR owner” access implied by its use.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The handler commits the new attendee rows via prisma.booking.update with attendees.createMany (lines 92-106) before the external calendar update (line 165) and email send (line 168) run, with no transaction, compensation, or attendee-removal path. adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The organizer is fetched with prisma.user.findFirstOrThrow({ where: { id: booking.userId || 0 } }) with no not-found handling, despite the author's own '|| 0' acknowledging userId can be null. adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The guests array has no .max() cap, so a single authorized request creates an unbounded number of attendee rows and triggers an unbounded number of outbound emails (organizer, every existing attendee, and every new guest is emailed per call). adjudication.rationale: The diff adds a new authed mutation `viewer.bookings.addGuests` with input schema `ZAddGuestsInputSchema` defined as `guests: z.array(z.string().email())` (packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.schema.ts) with no `.max(...)` or other server-side cap. adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The BAD_REQUEST thrown when uniqueGuests is empty reuses 'emails_must_be_unique_valid', but the actual condition is that every submitted guest was already an attendee or blacklisted — not that the emails are malformed or duplicated. adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The handler authorizes and executes addGuests without ever checking booking.status, so the flow runs on CANCELLED and REJECTED bookings.
